newsitem.title: USA: ARCO posts 31 percent increase in first-quarter profits.
newsitem.headline: ARCO posts 31 percent increase in first-quarter profits.

text.p: Atlantic Richfield Co. said Monday its first-quarter profits jumped by more than 30 percent as the company's strong 1996 performance continued into the first three months of this year.

The Los Angeles-based oil company said its net income for the three months ended March 31 expanded to $483 million, or $2.95 a share, from $370 million, or $2.26 a share, a year earlier. It was Arco's best first quarter in seven years.
Sales and operating revenues grew by 19 percent to $5 billion from $4.2 billion.
The company also said its board approved a 2-for-1 stock split and a 4 percent increase in the quarterly dividend, both effective June 13 for stockholders of record on May 16.
"We had the same strong performance level in the 1997 first quarter that we had for most of 1996, which was one of our best years ever," Chairman Mike R. Bowlin said in a statement.

"Our oil and gas business benefited from healthy prices, compared with last year's first quarter, while Arco's West Coast refining and marketing benefited from increased margins and volume growth. These improvements more than offset reduced income from Arco Chemical Co."
The company said higher crude oil and natural gas prices enabled its worldwide exploration and production operations to boost after-tax earnings to $452 million from $293 million.

It added that higher prices and stronger refined-product sales helped its refining and marketing segment to increase after-tax net earnings to $44 million from $28 million, offsetting the impact of increased crude oil prices.

Arco said after-tax earnings from its 82.6 percent interest in Arco Chemical Co. plunged to $50 million from $97 million as higher raw material costs coupled with weak product pricing compressed margins in virtually all business lines.
But the company also saw income from its 49.9 percent equity interest in Lyondell Petrochemical Co. expand to $30 million from $12 million.
Arco's stock added $1.875 to $135.75 in late trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
